figures.caption: Figure 3: Performance of COSMOS and heterogeneous-model baselines on CIFAR-100 under different mixtures of client architectures. Each subfigure corresponds to a distinct architecture combination. A statistical summary of the final communication round appears in Appendix D, Table 3.

Table 2: Final-round performance on benchmark datasets (mean ± SEM) under Dirichlet data heterogeneity with α = 5. Rows marked with † denote that COSMOS’s SEM error bar does not overlap with any baseline (COMET, FedCT, or FedMD). Figure 2 presents performance across communication rounds.

Figure 9: Top-1 accuracy over communication rounds for COSMOS. Subfigure (a) shows performance under different values of λ. Subfigure (b) shows performance on CIFAR-100 with Dirichlet non-IID sampling (α = 5) under varying distillation temperatures and different statistical aggregation rules (mean, median, max). Client models are MobileNet and SqueezeNet.

Table 8: Final-round performance of COSMOS under: (a) varying numbers of participating clients, (b) different ratios (fractions) of unlabeled global data, and (c) different server-side architectures.

Table 6: Final-round performance on benchmark datasets (mean ± SEM) under Dirichlet data heterogeneity with α = 100. Rows marked with † denote that COSMOS’s SEM error bar does not overlap with any baseline (COMET, FedCT, or FedMD). Figure 5. presents performance across communication rounds.

Figure 8: Top-1 accuracy over communication rounds for COSMOS showing the performance on CIFAR-100 with Dirichlet non-IID sampling (α = 5) under varying number of clusters (i.e., values of β shown in the legend), Client models are AlexNet.

Figure 6: Top-1 accuracy over communication rounds for homogeneous client architectures (AlexNet, ResNet, MobileNet, and SqueezeNet) on CIFAR-100 with Dirichlet non-IID partitioning (α = 5). Each curve shows the mean accuracy across seeds for a variety of algorithms that do not require clients to be model-agnostic: COMET, Ditto, FedBABU, FedMD, FedSelect, COSMOS, pFedCK, and pFedHN. A statistical summary of the final communication round appears in Table 7.

Figure 7: Top-1 accuracy over communication rounds for COSMOS on CIFAR-100 with Dirichlet non-IID sampling (α = 5): (a) varying numbers of participating clients, (b) different ratios (fractions) of unlabeled global data, and (c) different server-side architectures. Client models are MobileNet and SqueezeNet.
